title: Synthesis of Cationized Magnetoferritin for Ultra-fast Magnetization of Cells
protocol: Deoxygenate 500 ml of deionized water by bubbling nitrogen gas through it for approximately 60 min.
Synthesize magnetoferritin in a sealable, double-jacketed reaction vessel under a nitrogen atmosphere at 65 °C.
Inject metal salt solutions and hydrogen peroxide into the reaction vessel using a syringe pump.
Purify synthesized magnetoferritin by anion-exchange chromatography to remove nanoparticles not enclosed in the protein cavity.
Isolate protein monomers using size-exclusion chromatography.
Determine protein concentration using a Bradford assay.
Heat a water bath connected to the double jacketed reaction vessel to 65 °C.
Add 75 ml of 50 mM HEPES buffer (pH 8.6) into the reaction vessel.
Seal the reaction vessel.
Bubble nitrogen gas through the buffer solution for approximately 20 min.
Stir the buffer solution using a magnetic stirrer during deoxygenation.
Remove the tube supplying nitrogen gas from the buffer after deoxygenating.
Suspend the removed tube in the vessel to maintain a nitrogen atmosphere.
Add apo-ferritin to achieve a final concentration of 3 mg/ml.
Continue stirring with a magnetic stirrer, reducing speed if foaming occurs.
Prepare a 25 mM stock solution of cobalt sulfate heptahydrate by dissolving 0.19 g in 50 ml of deoxygenated deionized water.
Prepare a 25 mM solution of ammonium iron sulfate hexahydrate by dissolving 0.98 g in 100 ml of deoxygenated deionized water.
Remove 2.5 ml of the ammonium iron sulfate hexahydrate solution and replace with 2.5 ml of cobalt sulfate heptahydrate.

Prepare an 8.33 mM solution of hydrogen peroxide in deoxygenated deionized water by first adding 965 μl of a 30% w/w hydrogen peroxide solution to 9 ml of deoxygenated deionized water, and then diluting 1 ml with 99 ml of deoxygenated deionized water.
Inject 10.1 ml of both the iron-cobalt precursor and the hydrogen peroxide simultaneously into the apo-ferritin solution.
Deoxygenate another 500 ml of deionized water during the injection period.
Prepare another 100 ml of iron-cobalt precursor and hydrogen peroxide solution using freshly deoxygenated deionized water.
Repeat the injection step described in 1.3.1 using freshly prepared solutions of iron-cobalt and hydrogen peroxide.
Deoxygenate another 500 ml of deionized water during the injection period.
Leave the solution to mature for 15 min under stirring after the third injection.
Add 1.5 ml of a 1 M sodium citrate solution to the reaction vessel.
Remove the solution from the reaction vessel into 50 ml centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the solution for 30 min at 4,350 x g.
Pass the supernatant through a 0.22 µm syringe filter.
Store the filtered supernatant at 4 °C until purification.
Load the sample onto a column containing a cationic matrix using a peristaltic pump at a flow rate of 10 ml/min.
Wash the column with approximately 100 ml of running buffer (50 mM Tris, pH 8.0) using a gradient pump at a flow rate of 10 ml/min.
Elute the protein from the column by washing it with increasing concentrations of sodium chloride in Tris buffer: 150, 500, and 1,000 mM final NaCl concentration (150 ml each).
Collect eluted protein fractions at a 500 mM sodium chloride concentration.
Concentrate 150 ml of magnetoferritin to approximately 2 ml using a centrifugal filter unit.
Load the concentrated sample onto a gel filtration column using an injection loop.
Wash the gel filtration column with running buffer (50 mM Tris, pH 8.0 containing 150 mM NaCl) at a flow rate of 1.3 ml/min.
Collect 6 ml fractions from the gel filtration column.
Store purified magnetoferritin at 4°C for further use.
Prepare ferritin standards of 0.06, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, and 1 mg/ml in 50 mM Tris buffer using commercially available horse spleen ferritin.
Dilute magnetoferritin samples until the color matches the 0.5 mg/ml standard.
Note the dilution factor for each sample.
Add 10 μl of each standard and diluted magnetoferritin sample in triplicate into wells of a 96 well plate.
Add 200 μl of Bradford reagent to each well.
Incubate at room temperature for 8 minutes.
Measure absorbance at λ = 595 nm using a microplate reader.
Plot the mean absorbance of the ferritin standards as a function of protein concentration.
Calculate the concentration of the magnetoferritin sample using the slope and intercept of the linear fit, taking into account the dilution factor.
Dialyze magnetoferritin samples into 50 mM phosphate buffer containing 50 mM NaCl.
Adjust protein concentration of dialyzed magnetoferritin to 4 mg/ml.
Weigh out 374 mg of DMPA and dissolve in 2.5 ml of 200 mM MES buffer.
Adjust pH of DMPA solution to approximately 7 using concentrated HCl.
Add 2.5 ml of magnetoferritin solution at 4 mg/ml to the DMPA/MES buffer mixture.
Stir the mixture for 2 hours.
Carefully adjust the pH of the mixture to 5.0 using 1 M HCl.
Add 141 mg of EDC powder to the mixture.
Continue stirring for 3.5 hours.
Filter the solution through a 0.22 µm syringe filter to remove precipitates.
Seed 150,000 hMSCs into 25 cm² flasks and leave to adhere overnight at 37°C.
Filter sterilize cationized magnetoferritin through a 0.22 μm syringe filter.
Determine the protein concentration of cationized magnetoferritin.
Prepare a 0.5 μM solution of cationized magnetoferritin in phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Wash the plated cells with 2 ml of room temperature PBS.
Incubate plated cells with 1 ml of sterilized cationized magnetoferritin solution for the desired time period.
Wash cells with PBS.
Add 0.5 ml of trypsin/EDTA to harvested cells and incubate at 37 °C for 5 min.
Inactivate trypsin/EDTA by adding 1 ml of culture medium, transfer to a 15 ml centrifuge tube, and centrifuge for 5 min at 524 x g.
Discard the supernatant and re-suspend the cell pellet in 0.5 ml magnetic separation buffer.
Attach the magnet to the multi stand and add a magnetic separation column.
Place a pre-separation filter on the column.
Place 0.5 ml of magnetic separation buffer in the pre-separation filter, letting it run through both the filter and the column.
Place a 15 ml centrifuge tube under the column.
Add 0.5 ml of the cell suspension to the filter reservoir of the magnetic separation column.
When the reservoir is empty, add 0.5 ml of magnetic separation buffer.
Repeat one more time with another 0.5 ml of magnetic separation buffer.
The total volume used for washing should be 1.5 ml of magnetic separation buffer.
This step elutes all non-magnetized cells from the column (non-magnetized cell fraction).
Remove the column from the magnet.
Place the column in a fresh 15 ml centrifuge tube.
Add 1 ml of magnetic separation buffer to the reservoir.
Push through the column using the plunger supplied by the manufacturer.
Centrifuge both tubes for 5 min at 524 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Re-suspend the cell pellets in 0.3 ml PBS.
Count the number of cells in each fraction using a hemocytometer.
Determine the fraction of magnetized cells, M(%), using the equation provided.
Centrifuge a known number of cells for 5 min at 524 x g.
Remove the PBS supernatant.
Add 0.25 ml of 50% (v/v) nitric acid to each sample.
Vortex mix the acidified cell suspension.
Incubate the samples at room temperature overnight.
Add 4.75 ml of distilled water to each sample.
Vortex mix the diluted samples.
Analyze with ICP-OES.
Normalize the measured iron content to the number of cells to determine the cellular iron content.
